name: set
title: View or set environment variables in CMD
description: With no arguments it lists every environment variable. Assigning a value affects only the current Command Prompt session; use 'setx' to persist a variable.

examples.explanation: Lists every environment variable in the current session.
Sets a variable for this Command Prompt session only.

risk.sideEffects: Affects the current shell session only; changes vanish when it closes.

name: zip
title: Create a ZIP archive
description: Packages files into a compressed .zip archive. ZIP is the most portable choice when the recipient may be on Windows.

flags.name: -r
flags.description: Recurse into directories.
Maximum compression, which is slower.

flags.name: -e
flags.description: Encrypt the archive with a password prompt.

examples.explanation: Compresses the src directory into project.zip.

risk.sideEffects: Creates a new archive file; overwrites an existing archive of the same name.

name: gzip
title: Compress a single file with gzip
description: Compresses one file in place, replacing it with a .gz version. It handles a single file, not directories - use tar for a tree.

flags.name: -k
flags.description: Keep the original file instead of replacing it.

flags.name: -d
flags.description: Decompress instead of compress, equivalent to gunzip.
Best compression at the cost of speed.

examples.explanation: Creates app.log.gz while keeping the original file.
Decompresses the archive back to app.log.

risk.sideEffects: Without -k the original file is replaced by the compressed version.

name: pip install
title: Install Python packages
description: Installs packages from the Python Package Index into the active environment. Always activate a virtual environment first so you do not modify the system Python.

flags.name: -r
flags.description: Install every package listed in a requirements file.

flags.name: -U
flags.description: Upgrade the package to the latest version.

flags.name: -e
flags.description: Install a local project in editable mode.

examples.explanation: Installs the requests library into the active environment.
Installs every pinned dependency for the project.

risk.sideEffects: Downloads and executes package setup code; modifies the active Python environment.
risk.reversibility: Reversible with 'pip uninstall', though installed setup scripts may leave artifacts.

name: apt install
title: Install system packages on Debian and Ubuntu
description: Installs packages system-wide using the APT package manager. It requires root, and it can pull in or remove dependent packages as part of the operation.

flags.name: -y
flags.description: Assume yes to prompts, for non-interactive use.

flags.name: --no-install-recommends
flags.description: Skip recommended but non-essential packages.

examples.explanation: Installs the nginx package and its dependencies.

risk.sideEffects: Modifies system-wide software, may remove conflicting packages, and runs maintainer scripts as root.
risk.reversibility: Mostly reversible with 'apt remove', but configuration changes may persist.

name: brew install
title: Install packages with Homebrew on macOS
description: Installs a formula or cask using Homebrew. Unlike apt it does not normally require root, because Homebrew owns its own prefix.

flags.name: --cask
flags.description: Install a GUI application rather than a command-line formula.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.description: Show what would be installed without doing it.

examples.explanation: Installs the ripgrep command-line tool.

risk.sideEffects: Downloads and installs software into the Homebrew prefix; may upgrade dependencies.

name: docker exec
title: Run a command inside a running container
description: Executes a command in a container that is already running. With -it it opens an interactive shell, which is the usual way to inspect a live container.
aliases: get a shell in a container
run a command in a container

flags.name: -i
flags.description: Keep stdin open.

flags.name: -t
flags.description: Allocate a pseudo-TTY; combined with -i for an interactive shell.

flags.name: -u
flags.description: Run as a specific user inside the container.

examples.explanation: Opens an interactive bash shell inside the web container.
Lists a directory inside the container without opening a shell.

risk.sideEffects: Runs arbitrary commands inside the container, which can modify its filesystem.
risk.reversibility: Depends on what is run; container changes are lost when the container is recreated.

name: docker images
title: List local Docker images
description: Shows the images stored locally with their repository, tag, and size. Useful for finding what is consuming disk space.

flags.name: -a
flags.description: Include intermediate layer images.

flags.name: -q
flags.description: Print only image IDs.

examples.explanation: Lists all top-level local images with their sizes.

name: wc
title: Count lines, words, and bytes
description: Counts lines, words, characters, and bytes in files. Most often used with -l to answer 'how many lines is this file?'.

flags.name: -l
flags.description: Print the line count only.

flags.name: -w
flags.description: Print the word count only.

flags.name: -c
flags.description: Print the byte count only.

examples.explanation: Prints how many lines the log file contains.

name: less
title: View a file one page at a time
description: Opens a file in a scrollable pager without loading the whole file into memory, which makes it suitable for very large logs. Press q to quit and / to search.

flags.name: -N
flags.description: Show line numbers.

flags.name: +F
flags.description: Follow the file as it grows, like 'tail -f' but scrollable.

flags.name: -S
flags.description: Truncate long lines instead of wrapping them.

examples.explanation: Opens the log in a scrollable pager.
Follows new lines as they are written, with Ctrl+C to stop following.

name: top
title: Monitor running processes and resource usage
description: Shows a continuously updating view of processes ordered by CPU usage, along with overall memory and load. Press q to quit.

flags.name: -u
flags.description: Show only processes owned by a given user.

flags.name: -b
flags.description: Batch mode, suitable for redirecting output to a file.

flags.name: -n
flags.description: Exit after the given number of refreshes.

examples.explanation: Opens the interactive process monitor.
Prints a single non-interactive snapshot.

risk.sideEffects: Read-only monitoring. Interactive keys can signal processes, so avoid stray keypresses.

name: uname
title: Show system and kernel information
description: Prints the operating system name, kernel version, and machine architecture. Useful when you need to confirm which platform you are actually on.

flags.name: -a
flags.description: Print all available system information.

flags.name: -r
flags.description: Print the kernel release only.

flags.name: -m
flags.description: Print the machine hardware architecture.

examples.explanation: Prints complete system and kernel information.

name: uptime
title: Show how long the system has been running
description: Prints the current time, how long the machine has been up, the number of logged-in users, and the load averages over 1, 5, and 15 minutes.
aliases: how long has the server been up

flags.name: -p
flags.description: Print the uptime in an easy-to-read format.

flags.name: -s
flags.description: Print the time the system booted.

examples.explanation: Shows uptime together with the load averages.

name: which
title: Find which executable a command resolves to
description: Shows the full path of the executable that would run for a given command name. Essential when the wrong version of a tool is on PATH.

flags.name: -a
flags.description: Print every matching executable on PATH, not just the first.

examples.explanation: Prints the path of the node binary that would be executed.
Lists every python3 on PATH in resolution order.

name: where
title: Locate an executable on Windows
description: Searches PATH for a command and prints the full path of each match. The Windows counterpart to 'which'.
aliases: where is this program installed on windows

flags.name: /R
flags.description: Search recursively starting from a given directory.

examples.explanation: Prints the path of every node.exe found on PATH.
